title: Danbury City Council May 5, 2026 police-ordinance packet
summary: Primary municipal packet containing the proposed Article II Police Department amendments and the April 28 ad-hoc committee report.

evidence.claim: The packet identifies the amendment as Code of Ordinances sections 22-19 through 22-30; proposed section 22-27(a) expands police-applicant eligibility to U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and DACA recipients.
evidence.locator: proposed ordinance and April 28, 2026 ad-hoc report

caveats: This packet establishes the proposal and committee record; it is not by itself proof that the final enacted text was unchanged.

title: Danbury Police Department monthly report — March 2026
summary: Primary Danbury Police staffing report dated March 26, 2026 and included in the April City Council record.

evidence.claim: Chief Patrick Ridenhour reported 175 authorized sworn positions, 159 sworn personnel, and effective strength of 149 as of March 25, 2026.
evidence.locator: March 26, 2026 Police Department monthly report, Personnel section

evidence.claim: The report states that two Connecticut-certified officers confirmed January 6 had completed modified field training, one New York-certified officer was in comparative certification training, one entry-level recruit graduated March 18, and six entry-level recruits remained at the Milford Police Academy.
evidence.locator: March 26, 2026 Police Department monthly report, Personnel bullets

caveats: The report supplies counts and training states but does not name the January-certified officers or the academy recruits in the reviewed passage.

title: Danbury PD primary-record reconciliation — ordinance text and March 2026 staffing
summary: Primary City records resolve the exact proposed code sections and March staffing baseline while leaving final enacted/codified ordinance text and officer-name reconciliation open.

caveats: The May packet is proposal-stage evidence; the September adoption is independently reported, but this pass did not recover final enacted/codified text or an effective date.
Staff counts are a March 25 snapshot and must not be projected to September as current strength.

findings: The City record resolves the previously garbled section reference as Article II Police Department, Code sections 22-19 through 22-30, with applicant eligibility in proposed section 22-27(a).
The proposal-stage text explicitly includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and DACA recipients as eligible police applicants.
Danbury Police reported 175 authorized sworn positions, 159 sworn personnel, and effective strength 149 as of March 25, 2026.

The March personnel pipeline included two Connecticut-certified officers released to full duty, one New York-certified officer in comparative certification training, one March 18 academy graduate entering in-house/field training, and six recruits still at Milford Police Academy.
conclusions: Primary municipal evidence now supports the exact ordinance-section scope and March staffing denominator used by issue #2514.

The final enacted/codified ordinance text, effective date, and names of the January-certified/academy officers remain unresolved and should be joined from later council, Civil Service, appointment, academy, and personnel records rather than inferred.
counterarguments: The City police landing page has displayed a different authorized-strength figure; a current webpage figure and the dated FY25-26 monthly-report figure describe different source states and should not be silently collapsed.
Proposal language can change before enactment, so the May text is not promoted to final codified text without the September adoption/codification record.
unresolved: Final enacted ordinance text and codified section history after the September 2026 vote.
Ordinance effective date and formal ordinance/resolution identifier.
Names and present status of the two Connecticut-certified officers, one New York-certified officer, March 18 academy graduate, and six Milford academy recruits.
Full current sworn-force reconciliation against the 2025 payroll-derived candidate census and later 2026 departures/hiring.

title: Research pass: Danbury PD primary-record reconciliation (2026-09-15)
summary: Bounded issue #2514 pass recovering primary municipal ordinance and staffing evidence without treating proposal text as final codification or March counts as current September staffing.

data.research_question: Which primary City of Danbury records resolve the police-eligibility ordinance section scope and the sworn-force staffing baseline for issue #2514, and what remains unresolved?
data.method: Searched the existing corpus first, then reviewed official City of Danbury agenda/meeting records and Police Department monthly-report material. Preserved proposal-stage ordinance evidence separately from enactment and preserved the dated staffing snapshot separately from current-force claims.
classification_rules: Proposal text is not promoted to final enacted text without the final adoption/codification record.
Dated staffing counts are not projected forward as present-day staffing.
Unnamed recruits/officers remain unnamed; no identity inference from count or training status.
Only professional/public-record information is in scope; immigration status of individual officers is not inferred.

findings.finding: Official City material identifies Code sections 22-19 through 22-30 and proposed section 22-27(a) as the police-applicant eligibility amendment surface.

The March Police report establishes a primary-source 175 authorized / 159 sworn / 149 effective-strength snapshot as of March 25, 2026 and a seven-person entry-level academy pipeline plus comparative-certification activity.
